What are the equations of the horizontal asymptotes of $y=f(x)$ whose graph is shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
- On the right of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets larger and larger, the function $f(x)$ levels off to the value of $-3.$ We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to -3\,\text{as}\,x\to \infty 
$$

Therefore, $f(x)$ has a horizontal asymptote at $y=-3.$

- On the left of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets more and more negative, the function $f(x)$ levels off to the value of $2.$ We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to 2\,\text{as}\,x\to -\infty 
$$

Therefore, $f(x)$ also has a horizontal asymptote at $y=2.$

Which of the following statements are true for the graph shown above?

I. $f(x)\to 2$ as $x\to -\infty $

II. $f(x)\to 1$ as $x\to \infty $

III. $f(x)\to 0$ as $x\to -\infty $
questions.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement one-by-one.

- On the left of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets more and more negative, the function $f(x)$ levels off to the value of $2.$ We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to 2\,\text{as}\,x\to -\infty 
$$

Therefore, statement I is true while statement III is false.

- On the right of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets larger and larger, the function $f(x)$ levels off to the value of $1.$ We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to 1\,\text{as}\,x\to \infty 
$$

Therefore, statement II is true.

As a result, the correct answer is "I and II only".

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14250658/assets/c12deadd41a9c2853d0d2d50ba5c19ac6ca13012d7672941c92fa5e6cc5df642.png)

Which of the following statements are true for the graph shown above?

I. $y=-1$ is a horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$

II. $y=1$ is a horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$

III. $y=2$ is a horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's analyze each statement one-by-one.

- On the right of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets larger and larger, the function $f(x)$ levels off to the value of $1.$ We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to 1\,\text{as}\,x\to \infty 
$$

This means that $y=1$ is a horizontal asymptote of $f(x).$ Therefore, statement II is true.

- On the left of the graph, we see that as $x$ gets more and more negative, the function $f(x)$ levels off to the value of $2.$ We can express this as follows:

$$
f(x)\to 2\,\text{as}\,x\to -\infty .
$$

This means that $y=2$ is a horizontal asymptote of $f(x).$ Therefore, III is also true.

- The horizontal asymptotes of $f(x)$ are $y=1$ and $y=2.$ The line $y=-1$ is not a horizontal asymptote of $f(x)$ because the function does not level off to $-1$ on the right nor on the left. Therefore, I is false.

As a result, the correct answer is "II and III only".
